source: Chollet, Knoop, Kamradt, Landers (2026) ARC Prize 2025: Technical Report
finding: Top Kaggle score on ARC-AGI-2 private set was 24.03% at $0.20 per task. The authors say frontier reasoning is bound by knowledge coverage, and that ARC-AGI-1 and -2 are now partly overfit by models trained on public data. They cannot say if this is accidental or intentional, and they do not measure its size.
numbers: 1,455 teams, 15,154 entries. NVARC 24.03%, ARChitects 16.53%, MindsAI 12.64%. ARC-AGI-2 has 120 semi-private and 120 private tasks; each task solved by at least 2 of 2-10 human testers. Poetiq harness on Gemini 3 Pro: 31% at $0.81 per task to 54% at $31 per task; Claude Opus 4.5 similar accuracy at about $60 per task (Poetiq-reported).
quote: current frontier AI reasoning performance remains fundamentally constrained to knowledge coverage
limits: Contamination claim rests on one anecdote: Gemini 3 Deep Think used correct ARC color mappings (Green=3, Magenta=6) when the prompt gave only 2D integer arrays. No counterfactual or fresh-task measurement. Authors own the benchmark.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: memorisation is plausible but unquantified. Treat ARC-AGI-1 scores as upper bounds on novelty skill; prefer private or freshly made items for S0 tests.

source: Chollet et al. (2026) ARC Prize 2025 Technical Report, sections 3.3-3.4: refinement loops and token use
finding: Reasoning length varies hugely with item: on one ARC-AGI-1 task Gemini 3 Pro used 96 reasoning tokens and Gemini 3 Deep Think used 138,000. The report calls refinement loops (explore, verify, repeat with a feedback signal) the defining 2025 theme, including prompt-level harnesses on commercial models.
numbers: 96 vs 138,000 reasoning tokens on task 4cd1b7b2. Harness gain 31% to 54% on ARC-AGI-2 at about 38x cost. TRM (7M params) 45% ARC-AGI-1 and 8% ARC-AGI-2; CompressARC (76K params) about 20% ARC-AGI-1 and 4% ARC-AGI-2.
limits: Harness is domain specific (the ARC verifier is the training pairs). Cost is not matched across arms. Poetiq numbers are Poetiq-reported, then verified by ARC Prize.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: the best prompt-level scaffold on ARC-AGI-2 gains about 23 points, but only with a checkable verifier and 38x cost. Our schema needs a cost cap and a verifier test at S0.

source: Gema et al. (2025) Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute (TMLR)
finding: Longer reasoning lowers accuracy on several task types, including Zebra constraint puzzles (BIG-Bench Extra Hard). Model-chosen length shows stronger inverse scaling than a forced budget. Claude models get more distracted; o-series resist distractors but overfit familiar framings; R1 degrades most.
numbers: Misleading Math: 500 questions per distractor count n=1..5. R1 natural overthinking: 70% to 30% at 5 distractors. Claude Opus 4: near 100% falls to 85-90%. Zebra puzzles: 200 items, grids up to 8x8, limits 16k reasoning and 10k output tokens; R1 shows inverse scaling in all grid sizes; Opus 4 non-monotonic; o3 noisy, positive only on 8x8.
limits: Tasks are not abstract rule induction like ARC. Novelty is not varied on purpose. Length is binned within model, so it is confounded with item difficulty (partly handled by the controlled setup).
agent_relevance: Gap 2: direct warning against a longer-is-better rule. The longest Zebra traces show excess hypothesis testing and self-doubt. Supports a length cap and a restart rule, but no novelty-indexed curve exists.

source: Haznitrama, Ardi, Oh (2026) A Neuropsychologically Grounded Evaluation of LLM Cognitive Abilities (NeuroCognition)
finding: A Raven-style benchmark in text and image for 10 reasoning models. Models do better on text than image; humans the reverse. Turning reasoning off helps on 8-choice text matrices; reasoning helps on image items and free-form answers. Harder items lower scores.
numbers: RAPM: 140 image items (RAVEN dataset, 7 configurations x 20) and 200 generated text items. Modality effect on RAPM p=.010. Reasoning off vs on: Text MC gain p=.021; Text Gen p=.83 and Image MC p=.173 not significant. Human text pilot N=9: 0.430 (MC), 0.444 (Gen); human image 0.814 (Zhang et al.). GPT-5 Text 0.540 MC to 0.605 Gen; Claude 0.560 to 0.385. Factor analysis of 156 models: one factor 75% of variance, loadings above 0.76. NeuroCognition vs 11-benchmark average r=.86, p=.001, N=10 models.
limits: Tiny human samples (N=9, N=11). Human image norm is from another dataset paper, not matched. Reasoning disabled for Claude Sonnet 4 and Grok 4 Fast on RAPM because of overthinking. Text matrices are generated, not Raven norms.
agent_relevance: Gaps 2 and 9: a second source that long reasoning can hurt on matrix items with many answer options. Human Raven norms do not transfer: the image human norm cannot be applied to the text form.

source: Li, Hu, Larsen et al. (2024) Combining Induction and Transduction for Abstract Reasoning
finding: Trained models for induction (write a program that explains the examples) and transduction (predict the output directly) on ARC. They solve different problems; ensembling is best. Induction is better at precise computation and composing concepts; transduction at fuzzy perceptual concepts. What is hard for humans is not what is hard for the models.
numbers: ARC validation, 2 tries: ensemble 26.50% (GPT-4 descriptions) vs 19.50% (GPT-4o-mini descriptions); induction with 2048 samples 18.78% vs 11.07%; transduction beam 20 15.25% vs 13.50%. At scale (BARC): ensemble 56.75% with test-time training, against average human 60.2% and best human 97.8%; with Akyurek's TTT 61.9%. Five difficulty bins from LeGris et al.: all models beat humans on the hardest 20% and trail humans on the easiest 20%.
limits: Models are fine-tuned on synthetic ARC-like data, so not prompt-only. Some table rows are scrambled in the PDF text, so row-to-number mapping for the BARC rows is uncertain. Methods use different test-time compute.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1, 4, 5: human difficulty does not predict model difficulty, so a human-style novelty sort at S0 can misroute. Program induction checked against the given examples is a strong step; direct prediction is a complementary fallback.

source: Pourcel, Colas, Oudeyer (2026) SOAR: Self-Improving Language Models for Evolutionary Program Synthesis on ARC-AGI
finding: Search (sample many programs, refine from failures) lifts open models from near zero to 14-26%, and fine-tuning on the search traces lifts them to 36-45%. One-shot frontier models are low. Final 52% on the ARC-AGI-1 public test with majority voting.
numbers: One-shot ARC-test: Qwen-2.5-Coder 1.00-2.25%, GPT-4.1 8.00%, Claude-4-Sonnet 20.75%, o3-mini 38.25%, reasoners 33.00%. Sample-6k / Sample&Refine-6k / SOAR-6k: Qwen-14B 5.63 / 14.25 / 36.25; Qwen-72B 12.88 / 25.25 / 44.38; Mistral-Large-2 18.50 / 25.62 / 44.88; GPT-4.1 19.75 / 26.25 / 45.50. Peak 52.00% with voting, oracle 57.25%.
limits: Public ARC-AGI-1 test, the set the ARC Prize report calls partly contaminated. Needs thousands of samples per task and training compute. The demonstration pairs act as verifier.
agent_relevance: Gaps 5 and 6: hypothesis-as-program with an execution check works on current models, with large gains over one-shot at the same model, but at high sample cost. Gains come from sampling plus checking, not from one longer chain.

source: Hu, Cy, Qiu et al. (2025) ARC Is a Vision Problem! (VARC)
finding: Treating ARC as image-to-image translation with a plain Vision Transformer, trained from scratch plus test-time training, reaches LLM-level scores. The representation (pixels on a canvas, not text tokens) matters a great deal.
numbers: 18M-parameter VARC: 54.5% on ARC-1; 73M ensemble 60.4% on ARC-1 and 11.1% on ARC-2 (read from a scrambled table, row labels inferred). The paper says 60.4% matches reported average human on ARC-1. Table lists LLM leaderboard rows (e.g. GPT-5 7.8% ARC-2, DeepSeek R1 3.0 on ARC-2 by inference).
limits: Table text layout is garbled. Pass@2 with multi-view voting. Trained on ARC data.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: the best representation differs by model type (objects for LLMs, pixels for vision models), so no one rewrite step is robust. Try two renderings per item and keep the one that passes the demonstration pairs.

source: Jolicoeur-Martineau (2025) Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks (TRM)
finding: A 7M-parameter two-layer recursive network that refines its own answer for up to 16 supervision steps scores above most LLMs on ARC without language pretraining.
numbers: 7M parameters; 45% ARC-AGI-1 and 8% ARC-AGI-2; the abstract compares with Gemini 2.5 Pro at 4.9% on ARC-AGI-2 and says it uses less than 0.01% of the parameters.
limits: Trained on ARC-style data with heavy augmentation. Training compute is not small.
agent_relevance: Novelty skill is not tied to model scale; supports iterative answer refinement as an operator instead of a bigger model.

source: Xie, Huang, Zhang et al. (2025) On Memorization of Large Language Models in Logical Reasoning (Knights and Knaves)
finding: A controlled test of memorisation versus reasoning. Fine-tuned models reach near-perfect accuracy on training puzzles but fail on small perturbations; fine-tuning also raises accuracy on unseen puzzles, so memorisation and skill grow together.
numbers: Memorisation score (LiMem) above 50% on 8-person training puzzles under perturbation; near-zero accuracy on role-flipped puzzles (knight defined as liar), LiMem about 80% for Llama3-8B under role flip; math-level perturbations hurt less than language-level ones; harder puzzles give higher memorisation.
limits: Synthetic Knights and Knaves puzzles, not ARC. Fine-tuned models, not zero-shot prompting. Says nothing about how much of an ARC score is memorised.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: gives a method (consistency under local perturbation) for testing memorisation on our own items: re-score each item with a changed surface form and count items solved only in the original form.

source: Huang, Sun, Wang, Dredze (2026) On the Failure of Latent State Persistence in Large Language Models
finding: LLMs cannot keep an unwritten hidden choice stable across questions: probability mass over the state space does not sum to one, answers drift as questions accumulate, and hidden-variable tracking fails when the start state is not in context. The authors call LLMs reactive post-hoc solvers.
numbers: Three experiments (Number Guessing Game, Yes-No Game, Mathematical Mentalism). Partial figures seen: one model PR 0% with MSC 41.43, GPT-4o PR 13.5% with MSC 74.55. Full result tables not extracted.
limits: Abstract, setup and part of the results read. This is a latent-state test, not a Gf test; no link to Raven or ARC scores is shown.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: the limit is state not written down, not item count in context. Put every held item and hypothesis in written notes instead of trusting the model to carry it.

source: Haznitrama et al. (2026) NeuroCognition: Spatial Working Memory results
finding: Humans and LLMs fail differently on working-memory-like tasks. Humans forget; LLMs given the full history fail to use it. With history in context some models still drop near zero on hard image items.
numbers: Humans on image spatial WM: 0.963 easy, 0.878 hard (N=11), near ceiling with history. Gemini 3 Pro 1.00 easy, 0.79 hard; Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.41 easy over 3 runs. GPT-5 0.631 to 0.989 when text is added to image. Model effect size eta-squared .88 vs human participant .47.
limits: Small human N=11; spatial WM is not Gf. Three runs per model.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: LLM limits do not look like a human item-count capacity; they are failures to use stored state and run-to-run inconsistency. Design: solve twice and treat disagreement as low confidence.

source: Gema et al. (2025) Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute: controlled versus natural budgets
finding: The paper runs two regimes: controlled (prompted budget) and natural (model decides). Natural length shows the stronger inverse trend, so the model's own sense of how long to think is worse than an external cap.
numbers: Takeaway 5: natural overthinking gives stronger inverse scaling than controlled on Zebra puzzles. A cautioned-prompt variant was also run (Figures 28-29) and Claude models changed behavior across prompt setups.
limits: Reasoning-token axis is binned within model, so item difficulty is mixed in. No novelty variable.
agent_relevance: Gap 2: partly answered. Evidence for an external cap plus restart, not for a novelty-indexed curve.

source: Hu and Lewis (2025) critique of n-back as LLM working-memory test (ACL), search snippet only
finding: Search summary says Hu and Lewis question reading LLM n-back drops (GPT-3.5 worse at 2-back and 3-back) as human-like working-memory limits.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: treat human-style working-memory-limit analogies for LLMs as unproven.

source: Backward digit span benchmark for LLMs with text Raven and ARC-AGI-1 correlation (eScholarship qt28m3k4g4), snippet only
finding: Search summary says LLM backward-digit-span accuracy falls as sequence length grows, and that a text Raven task correlated with two fluid measures (Raven and ARC-AGI-1).
numbers: No numbers read; the PDF and item page could not be fetched.

source: Horn and Cattell (1967) Age differences in fluid and crystallized intelligence, Acta Psychologica 26:107-129
finding: Not read. Publisher link redirects without text. Secondary summaries say crystallized scores are higher in older adults and fluid scores higher in younger adults, and that omnibus IQ hides these opposite trends.
numbers: Sample sizes and Gf loadings not found in any opened source.
limits: Citation confirmed through Crossref metadata only. Cattell 1943 (Psychological Bulletin) also not obtained.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open; the claim that Gf peaks near 27 stays secondhand.

source: Li et al. (2024) Combining Induction and Transduction: human versus model difficulty on ARC
finding: On ARC, model strength and human strength are anti-aligned at both ends of the difficulty range. This weakens the idea that an S0 gate based on human-perceived novelty predicts model success.
numbers: Five equal difficulty bins from LeGris et al.: models above humans in the hardest bin, below humans in the easiest; mid-range roughly tracks human accuracy.
limits: Result is for fine-tuned code-trained transformers; may differ for prompt-only frontier models.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: an S0 sort should use a model-based difficulty signal (pilot attempt, disagreement across samples), not a human novelty rating.
